newsitem.title: USA: Losing bid on N.J. toll deal wants records - paper.
newsitem.headline: Losing bid on N.J. toll deal wants records - paper.

text.p: The losing bidder for New Jersey's $500 million electronic toll collection system asked a state panel to unseal records involved in the bidding, the Star Ledger reported Tuesday.
Lockheed Martin IMS, a unit of Lockheed Martin Corp, asked a state Appellate Division panel to unseal the documents used in selecting MFS Network Technologies to build the system.
The move came after reports that a consultant on the project wrote a memo supporting Lockheed's contention that the firm was misled about the importance of including a fiber-optic system in its bid.
The panel is scheduled on May 28 to hear arguments on Lockheed's challenge to the MFS award.
